memory: On 2024-11-08 at 15:30:00, Robert Thompson (owner) had a 49-minute veterinary consultation (conversation_id=vet_consult_001) with Dr. Sarah Mitchell at Companion Animal Hospital's Veterinary Services department regarding his dog Max.

Max is a 7-year-old Golden Retriever weighing 78 pounds (ideal weight 72-73 pounds) with a history of mild hip dysplasia diagnosed ~18 months prior (last X-ray then). As of the consultation, Max had a 2-week gradual limp on his right rear leg and reduced energy, with no known injury cause.

Max's current medications/supplements: Cosequin DS glucosamine (2 tablets daily with food), previously effective but no longer. Dr. Mitchell recommended adding Rimadyl (75mg twice daily) pending blood work, and starting omega-3 fish oil (7000-8000mg daily, brands Nordic Naturals/Grizzly Salmon Oil, $30-40/month) immediately with food to avoid stomach upset.

Max's diet: Hill's Science Diet Adult Large Breed, 3.5 cups/day split into 2 meals (morning/evening). Dr. Mitchell advised reducing to 3 cups/day and limiting treats to 10% of calories, suggesting low-calorie alternatives (baby carrots/green beans).

Scheduled visit: Max is to be brought to Companion Animal Hospital on 2024-11-09 at 9 AM (clinic open 8 AM-2 PM Saturdays) for fasting blood work (no food after 10 PM 2024-11-08), including complete blood count, chemistry panel, urinalysis ($285); hip/leg X-rays ($420); exam fee ($65); DHPP vaccine ($42, expired since 2024-10-30); heartworm test ($47, due annually despite current Heartgard Plus use). Total cost: $859. Visit duration ~2 hours, pickup ~11 AM.
Vaccination status: Max's rabies vaccine is current until March 2025; DHPP vaccine expired on 2024-10-30 and is to be administered at the scheduled visit.

Exercise recommendations: Current 45-minute walks twice daily → switch to 20-minute walks three times daily. Swimming (15-20 minutes, 2-3x weekly) at a heated dog pool was recommended (cost options: $25/session or $80/month unlimited).

Long-term treatment options: Depending on X-ray results, consider Adequan injections (loading dose: twice weekly for 4 weeks, $680 total; maintenance: monthly $85) or oral supplement Dasuquin Advanced ($75/month).
